title: Synthesis of protein conjugates adsorbed on cationic liposomes surface
author: Chatzikleanthous, Cunliffe, et al.

steps.title: Introduce maleimide groups onto protein
steps.instruction: Dissolve 1.52 mg EMCS in 50 µL DMSO; add 11 µL of this solution (6 eq‑v) to 1 mL of protein solution (6 mg total protein: for CRM197 use 130 µL of 47.4 mg/mL stock, for NadA use 860 µL of 7 mg/mL stock, for GBS67 use 330 µL of 18.4 mg/mL stock) prepared in 100 mM sodium phosphate, 1 mM EDTA, pH 8.1. Incubate 3 h at room temperature.

steps.title: Purify and characterize protein‑EMCS
steps.instruction: Purify the reaction mixture with 30 kDa VivaSpin 0.5 mL filter units, performing five diafiltration cycles against 50 mM sodium phosphate, 1 mM EDTA, pH 7.5. Determine protein concentration by BCA assay. Analyze linker‑to‑protein molar ratio by MALDI‑TOF: mix 2.5 µL product with 2.5 µL sinapinic acid matrix, spot 2.5 µL on a MALDI plate, dry 10 min at room temperature, then acquire linear positive‑ion spectrum.

steps.title: Synthesize CpG ODN‑SH (SPDP coupling)
steps.instruction: Dissolve 20 mg (3.21 µmol) CpG ODN 1826 (MW 6238) and 10 mg (32.1 µmol, 10 eq‑v) SPDP linker in 1 mL of 1:9 (v/v) 100 mM sodium phosphate, pH 7.2 : DMSO. Incubate 3 h at room temperature with continuous mixing.

substeps.instruction: Purify the reaction by size‑exclusion chromatography on a G25 Sephadex column eluting with H₂O; combine CpG‑containing fractions and concentrate using a Genevac evaporator.
Confirm linker incorporation by ¹H NMR.
Reduce the SPDP‑protected ODN by adding 3 eq‑v of 0.0005 M TCEP solution; incubate 3 h at room temperature in the dark.
Purify the reduced CpG‑ODN‑SH again on a G25 Sephadex column with H₂O as eluent.
Quantify recovered CpG‑ODN‑SPDP by measuring absorbance at 260 nm.

steps.title: Formulate cationic DSPC/Cholesterol/DDA liposomes
steps.instruction: Prepare a lipid stock in ethanol containing DSPC, cholesterol and DDA at a 10:40:50 molar ratio (2.88 mg/mL DSPC, 5.63 mg/mL cholesterol, 11.49 mg/mL DDA). Using a NanoAssemblr microfluidic mixer, inject the lipid stock and an aqueous phase of 10 mM Tris, pH 7.4 at a 1:1 (v/v) flow‑rate ratio, total flow rate 12 mL/min, to obtain liposomes at an initial lipid concentration of 20 mg/mL. Collect 1 mL of the liposome suspension and dialyze against 10 mM Tris, pH 7.4 for 1 h with magnetic stirring to remove residual ethanol.

steps.title: Adsorb protein‑CpG conjugate onto liposomes
steps.instruction: Mix the prepared liposomes with the protein‑CpG ODN conjugate at a weight‑to‑weight ratio of 1:20 (protein:liposome) in 10 mM Tris, pH 7.4. Prepare control samples containing liposomes with free protein alone or with free protein plus free CpG ODN. Incubate the mixtures 30 min at room temperature.

substeps.instruction: Dialyze the mixtures using Biotech CE tubing (300 kDa MWCO) overnight at 4 °C, performing two buffer exchanges, to remove unbound protein.
Determine the amount of protein remaining in the dialysate by BCA assay and the amount of CpG ODN by UV absorbance at 260 nm.
Calculate the amount of protein adsorbed on the liposome surface by subtracting the protein remaining in solution from the initial protein added.

steps.title: Conjugate CpG ODN‑SH to protein‑EMCS
steps.instruction: After TCEP reduction, incubate the CpG ODN‑SH with the purified protein‑EMCS to allow thiol‑maleimide coupling (reaction time and temperature as previously described for similar adjuvant‑protein conjugates).

substeps.instruction: Analyze the resulting protein‑CpG conjugates by SDS‑PAGE.

Perform SEC‑HPLC using a TSKgel G4000SW column (300 × 7.8 mm, 500 Å, 5 µm) with a flow rate of 0.5 mL/min, run time 45 min, and mobile phase consisting of 100 mM sodium phosphate, 100 mM Na₂SO₄, 5 % acetonitrile, pH 7.1. Inject 50 µL of sample at 0.5 mg/mL protein concentration.
